rows.description: A young adult sends a voice note to an ill or homesick relative and the warmth of the voice comforts more than a message. Elders in particular often prefer hearing over reading.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A person angry at a friend records a raw voice note and sends it before calming down. The tone stays permanent and replayable, so cooling off before recording matters.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A person keeps voice notes short, sums up the main point first, and asks whether the other has time. Considerate use respects the receiver's attention and setting.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager finds that classmates made another group chat without them and sees screenshots of their messages shared. Being left out or discussed behind their back stings deeply.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student watches classmates mock one member's message with laughing emojis and says nothing. Bystander silence lets pile-ons grow, and a simple change of topic or private support helps.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A member posts dozens of forwards, memes and good-morning messages, filling a family or college group. Many quiet members mute the chat and miss important information.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A professional keeps work chat clear and short, avoids sarcasm and moves sensitive discussion to a private call. Anything written may be screenshotted and read out of context.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A person who wants out of a noisy group mutes it or tells the admin they are stepping back for focus. Leaving silently can seem like an insult in close-knit circles, so a brief note eases it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A toddler in a bilingual household uses Hindi and English words in one sentence and switches freely. Mixing at this age is normal and does not confuse the child.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child speaks Hindi or a local dialect with grandparents and English at school, sensing which fits where. Reading the room by language is an early social skill.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
